intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm where tree roots swallow ancient stones.

experiences.name: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha adorned with 9,584 diamonds. Stroll along the nearby Sisowath Quay riverfront and explore the National Museum of Cambodia to deepen your understanding of Khmer history and art.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine Koh Rong Samloem island and spend the day on Saracen Bay, one of Southeast Asia's most unspoiled beaches. Snorkel among vibrant coral reefs, swim in crystal-clear turquoise waters, and witness magical bioluminescent plankton glowing in the sea after dark.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Street Food and Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening walk through the bustling Russian Market and Central Market, sampling authentic Khmer street food including fish amok, nom banh chok noodles, lok lak beef, and fresh sugarcane juice. Learn about the cultural significance of Cambodian cuisine and its French colonial influences.
experiences.location: Toul Tom Poung (Russian Market), Phnom Penh

experiences.name: Kampot River Kayaking and Pepper Farm Tour
experiences.description: Kayak along the serene Kampot River surrounded by lush jungle and karst mountains, then visit a world-renowned Kampot pepper farm to learn about the cultivation of Cambodia's prized export. Explore the charming French colonial architecture of Kampot town and enjoy sunset views over the Bokor Mountains.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect luggage. Take a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park (negotiate fare, expect $3–5 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate hotel area to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Ticket Office to purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass (1-day $37, 3-day $62, 7-day $72 — choose based on your plan; 3-day recommended for budget value).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Phsar Chas) area in central Siem Reap via tuk-tuk ($2–3). Browse the night market stalls, soak in the atmosphere, and pick up a cheap local SIM card if needed. Enjoy a relaxed first evening exploring the street food scene.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a local noodle soup (kuy teav) near the hotel for $1.50–2
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — authentic Khmer dishes like amok curry and lok lak for $3–5 per dish. Budget $6–8 total.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD at the airport or withdraw from an ATM (USD is widely accepted in Cambodia). Agree on tuk-tuk fares before riding. Keep arrival day light — rest is important after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM wake-up) and head to Angkor Wat for sunrise — one of the most iconic experiences in Southeast Asia. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a spot by the reflection pool. After sunrise, spend the morning exploring the vast temple complex of Angkor Wat itself: the outer galleries, the bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epic Mahabharata, and the central towers. Hire a local guide at the gate for $15–20 for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or tuk-tuk to Angkor Thom (the Great City), the last capital of the Khmer Empire. Explore the South Gate with its iconic naga balustrade, then visit the Bayon Temple — famous for its 216 serene stone faces. Afterward, see the Baphuon temple and stroll along the Elephant Terrace and Terrace of the Leper King.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenir shopping (silk scarves, carvings, handmade goods) — bargain respectfully. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant (some offer free shows with dinner).

meals.breakfast: Pack a baguette and fruit from a street vendor near the hotel before heading out ($1–2) — French baguettes are a Cambodian breakfast staple
meals.lunch: Local rice dish (bai sach chrouk — pork and rice) from a roadside stall near Angkor Thom for $1.50–2.50
meals.dinner: Dinner at Genevieve's Restaurant or a similar local spot near the night market — Khmer red curry with rice for $4–6. Fresh coconut water $1.

day_by_day.notes: Use your Angkor pass purchased on Day 1. Wear light, breathable clothing but bring a scarf to cover shoulders/knees at temples (required). Carry at least 1.5 liters of water — November can still be warm (~28–32°C). Tuk-tuk for the full Angkor temple loop costs $12–15 for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the 'Small Circuit' temples. Start with Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously left partially unrestored, with massive tree roots engulfing ancient stone walls (made famous by the Tomb Raider film). Arrive early to beat crowds. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a Buddhist temple with intricate carvings, and the peaceful Srah Srang reservoir — perfect for quiet reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan, a large flat temple complex with long corridors and atmospheric moss-covered stones. Then head to Neak Pean, a small artificial island temple built on a circular pond. End with Ta Som, a compact and charming temple with a tree-consumed eastern gopura. These lesser-visited temples offer a more peaceful experience than Angkor Wat.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, visit the Cambodian Cultural Village (entry ~$10) for an evening cultural show featuring traditional music, dance, and historical recreations of Khmer life — great for history and culture lovers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel (if included) or grab a bowl of congee (rice porridge) from a street stall for $1
meals.lunch: Pack lunch or buy from temple food stalls — fried rice with egg for $2–3
meals.dinner: Try Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer food for $5–8 per dish. Highly recommended.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your Angkor pass if you purchased a 3-day pass. Rent a bicycle from your hotel or a nearby shop ($2–4/day) to explore the smaller circuit independently — it's flat terrain and manageable. Bring sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily detailed pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. The intricate reliefs of Hindu deities and mythological scenes are breathtaking. Hire a tuk-tuk for the round trip ($12–15).
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Landmine Museum (free/donation), founded by a former child soldier. It's a sobering and deeply important cultural and historical experience that sheds light on Cambodia's tragic recent history. Then visit the nearby Elephant Jungle Sanctuary for a short ethical elephant observation walk (book in advance, ~$30–40 — splurge-worthy for ethical wildlife experience).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) in Siem Reap — watch skilled craftspeople recreate traditional Khmer silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerware. Great for understanding living cultural heritage. Browse their fair-trade shop.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake from a street stall — a backpacker classic in Southeast Asia, $1–1.50
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local market or eat at a roadside restaurant near Banteay Srei for $2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner at Psar Leu Market (local market) — eat where the locals eat. Fish amok or stir-fried morning glory for under $2. Authentic and budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: Use Day 3 of your Angkor pass if you have a 3-day pass (Banteay Srei is included). Start early for Banteay Srei — it gets hot and crowded by mid-morning. The Landmine Museum is sobering but essential for understanding modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Book with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — reliable, air-conditioned, and budget-friendly ($9–12, ~5–6 hours). Depart around 7:00–7:30 AM. Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse near the Riverside area (dorms $5–8/night, private rooms $12–18). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex ($10 entry). Marvel at the Khmer-style architecture, the Throne Hall, and the Silver Pagoda's floor of 5,000 silver tiles and golden Buddha statues.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) — the scenic waterfront boulevard along the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Watch the sunset over the river. Browse the riverside restaurants and bars. Visit the Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) for a sunset drink with a river view (budget for one drink ~$3–5).

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the bus — grab a baguette with pâté from a street vendor ($1) or eat at the bus station
meals.lunch: Snacks on the bus or stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey ($2–3)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends the Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training street youth. Try the tapas-style Khmer dishes. Budget $6–10.

day_by_day.notes: Book the bus ticket at least a day in advance. Store large bags in the bus hold. Phnom Penh is more urban and traffic-heavy than Siem Reap — use PassApp (local ride-hailing app) for affordable tuk-tuks and motodops. Download it before leaving Siem Reap.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. This is one of the most important and emotionally powerful historical sites in Southeast Asia. Entry is $5. Hire an audio guide or local survivor guide for deeper context. Allow 2–3 hours. This is a deeply sobering experience — approach with respect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Choeung Ek Genocidal Center — the infamous 'Killing Fields' located about 15 km south of the city (tuk-tuk ~$5–7 round trip). The audio guide ($6) is exceptional and narrates the site's harrowing history. Pay respects at the memorial stupa containing the remains of victims. This, combined with S-21, provides a comprehensive understanding of Cambodia's 1975–1979 tragedy.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and visit the Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) for affordable souvenirs, clothing, and local goods. Then head to the Night Market on Sisowath Quay — live music, street food, and a lively local atmosphere perfect for a Saturday evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or nearby café — eggs, toast, and coffee for $2–3
meals.lunch: Eat near Tuol Sleng — local noodle shop bun (rice vermicelli with fish-based broth) for $1.50–2
meals.dinner: Street food at the Night Market — grilled corn, skewers, noodles, and fresh spring rolls. Budget $3–5 for a full street food dinner.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time, be respectful, and allow yourself space to process. Photography is permitted in some areas but always with sensitivity. Avoid visiting these sites if you are emotionally vulnerable — but they are historically essential.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome built in 1937, one of the largest markets in Asia. Browse the stalls selling jewelry, watches, clothing, fresh produce, and local snacks. Great for people-watching and understanding everyday Cambodian commerce. Then visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name. Entry $1. Great city views from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip on the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers (organized tours ~$8–12, or negotiate a private boat for $10–15). See the confluence of the four rivers (Chaktomuk), spot local fishing villages, and enjoy the breezy river scenery. Alternatively, visit the National Museum of Cambodia ($10 entry) — an outstanding collection of Khmer art and sculpture spanning 1,000 years of history.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day preparation: Pack bags and book your onward bus/transport to Sihanoukville (for beach days). Enjoy a final Phnom Penh dinner along the riverside. Catch a traditional shadow puppet performance if available at local cultural venues.

meals.breakfast: Dim sum-style breakfast at the Central Market food stalls — dumplings and congee for $1.50–2
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the National Museum — fish amok set meal for $4–5
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner at a budget riverside restaurant — grilled prawns and Khmer salad with a Angkor beer for $7–10 total

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings are lively at Wat Phnom with local worshippers. Book your Sihanoukville bus ticket today for tomorrow morning — Giant Ibis or Larryta Express are recommended ($9–12, ~5 hours). Phnom Penh has excellent ATMs and pharmacies — stock up on any supplies before heading to the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bus from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (depart ~7:00 AM, arrive ~12:00–1:00 PM). Enjoy the changing landscape from city to coast. Upon arrival, take a tuk-tuk to your beach accommodation (budget guesthouses near Otres Beach: $10–20/night for private room). Otres Beach is quieter, cleaner, and more budget-friendly than Serendipity Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: First beach afternoon! Head straight to Otres Beach — a long, relatively unspoiled stretch of golden sand with calm turquoise water. Rent a beach chair ($1–2) and simply relax, swim, and decompress after days of temple and city exploration. The sea is warm in November (~28°C) and generally calm.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Otres Beach — one of Cambodia's finest sunset spots. As the sky turns orange and pink over the Gulf of Thailand, enjoy a cold Angkor beer from a beach bar ($1). Stroll along the beach and choose a restaurant for dinner from the laid-back beachside spots.

meals.breakfast: Snacks on the bus — bring food from Phnom Penh or buy at the bus station
meals.lunch: Grab a quick meal near the bus terminal upon arrival in Sihanoukville — fried rice for $2
meals.dinner: Beachside BBQ dinner at an Otres Beach restaurant — grilled fish, squid, or prawns with rice for $5–8. Fresh seafood is the highlight here.

day_by_day.notes: Sihanoukville has undergone significant development in recent years — Otres Beach area remains the most pleasant and budget-friendly zone for independent travelers. Avoid the main Serendipity/Victory Beach area which is heavily commercialized. November is a good month for the beach — end of rainy season means calmer seas and fewer crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to one of Cambodia's beautiful offshore islands. Koh Rong Samloem is highly recommended — a pristine island with crystal-clear water, white sand beaches, and minimal development. Ferry from Sihanoukville port (~$25–30 round trip, 45 min). Arrive at Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay and enjoy snorkeling, swimming, and island exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Koh Rong Samloem — snorkel around the coral reefs (rent gear for $5–8), hike the jungle trail across the island to the other beach, or simply lounge on the powdery white sand. The water here is exceptionally clear and rich in marine life including colorful fish and coral. If budget allows, take a sunset snorkeling trip ($10–15).
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Sihanoukville by late afternoon (last ferries usually around 4:30–5:00 PM — confirm schedule). Back in Sihanoukville, enjoy a quiet evening at Otres Beach. If you stay overnight on the island (budget bungalows from $15–25), enjoy the famous bioluminescent plankton in the water after dark — a magical natural phenomenon.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your guesthouse before heading to the ferry port — toast and eggs $2
meals.lunch: Lunch on the island — fresh coconut ($1.50) and a simple seafood plate at an island shack restaurant ($5–7)
meals.dinner: Back in Sihanoukville: dinner at a local Khmer restaurant away from the tourist strip — fish soup and rice for $3–4

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets the day before at the port or through your guesthouse to secure a spot. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag for electronics, and cash (ATMs are limited on the island). If you opt to stay overnight on the island, budget bungalows are available — a special experience for stargazing and bioluminescence.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Otres Beach — enjoy a slow, peaceful morning. Take a last swim in the Gulf of Thailand, walk along the beach, and collect any last memories. Visit the Otres Village area for a final browse of small local shops and artisan stalls. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — handmade bracelets, silk items, and local handicrafts are affordable here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap for your departure flight (confirm your return flight details). Bus from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh takes ~5 hours ($9–12). If flying out of Phnom Penh, depart Sihanoukville by noon at the latest. Use travel time to reflect on the journey, organize photos, and rest. If time allows before your flight, visit a final café in Phnom Penh for a Cambodian iced coffee (café toek doh ko) — a sweet, strong, and iconic farewell drink.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Cambodia. If your flight is the next day, book a final night at a budget guesthouse near the airport ($10–15). Spend the evening reviewing your incredible 10-day journey through the temples of Angkor, the history of Phnom Penh, and the beaches of Sihanoukville.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast — baguette with butter and condensed milk coffee at a beach café for $2–3
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a roadside stop during the bus journey or pack snacks
meals.dinner: Airport area dinner or a final Phnom Penh meal — Khmer BBQ (sach ko ang) with sticky rice for $4–6 as a farewell feast

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and airport transfer well in advance. Budget summary for the 10 days: Accommodation ~$80–130, Transport ~$60–80, Food ~$80–100, Activities/Entrance Fees ~$80–100, Miscellaneous ~$30–40. Estimated total: $330–450 USD for 10 days — very achievable on a budget. Always keep $20–30 USD emergency cash separate from your main wallet.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After settling in, take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor village area to acclimatize. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum (about 15 minutes from most Angkor-area hotels) for a superb introduction to Khmer history and the Angkor civilization — perfect for orienting yourself before temple visits.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap's Old Market (Psar Chas) area for a gentle first evening. Explore the vibrant Pub Street and surrounding lanes, browse local handicraft stalls, and soak up the atmosphere of this charming town.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a café near your hotel upon check-in — try a simple Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) for around $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or The Sugar Palm in Siem Reap Old Town — both offer authentic Khmer cuisine in a warm setting. Expect $10–18 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD or withdraw Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Purchase your Angkor Pass (1-day, 3-day, or 7-day) online or at the official ticket office — a 3-day pass ($62 USD) is recommended for this itinerary. Tuk-tuks from the airport to Angkor area hotels cost around $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Early start at Angkor Wat (arrive by 5:30–6:00 AM) to witness the legendary sunrise over the iconic temple reflected in the lotus ponds. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics like the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and climbing to the upper terraces. This is the world's largest religious monument and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a midday break, visit Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Explore the South Gate with its iconic stone faces, the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Terrace of the Elephants, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Hire your tuk-tuk driver to loop through the complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel for a refreshing shower and rest. Then head to Siem Reap Night Market or Angkor Night Market for dinner and light souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack or coffee from a vendor near Angkor Wat's entrance before sunrise ($2–4 USD). Have a proper breakfast at your hotel or a nearby café after sunrise.
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin or Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — try Amok (Khmer fish curry in coconut milk) for $5–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or a local restaurant near the Night Market. Try Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with lime pepper sauce). Budget $10–15 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start Day 2 very early (5:00 AM wake-up) for the Angkor Wat sunrise — this is one of Cambodia's most iconic experiences. Bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. Modest dress (covered shoulders and knees) is required at all temples. Your Angkor Pass (Day 1 of use) covers all sites today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple famously left partially unrestored, with giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees growing through its stone walls. The interplay of nature and ancient architecture is breathtaking. Arrive early (8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Afterward, explore the nearby Banteay Kdei temple and the serene Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan — a large, complex temple built by Jayavarman VII, featuring long colonnaded corridors, shrines, and beautiful carvings. Then explore Ta Som, a smaller but beautifully atmospheric temple with a famous tree-engulfed eastern gopura. End with a walk around the Neak Pean artificial island temple.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Apsara dance performance at Smile of Angkor Show or Aspara Theatre — a stunning cultural performance depicting Khmer classical dance, mythology, and history. This is a must-do cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at a local café near the Angkor area ($4–7 USD). Try Num Banh Chok (Khmer rice noodles with green curry) — a traditional Cambodian breakfast.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local market or eat at one of the food stalls near the temple complex. Simple rice dishes or noodles for $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner included or adjacent to the Apsara performance venue, or dine at Malis Restaurant for upscale Khmer cuisine ($15–22 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your Angkor Pass. The 'Grand Circuit' covers today's temples — ask your tuk-tuk driver to follow this route. Apsara dance show tickets cost approximately $25–35 USD and should be booked in advance. November weather in Siem Reap is typically dry season with pleasant temperatures (25–32°C).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century pink sandstone temple is renowned for having the finest and most intricate stone carvings of any Angkor-era temple. The detail and artistry are extraordinary. Combine with a visit to the nearby Banteay Samré temple on the return journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Landmine Museum (Aki Ra's Mine Museum) — a sobering and important cultural stop that educates visitors about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines and the ongoing humanitarian work to clear them. Then explore the Artisans Angkor workshop in Siem Reap, where you can watch skilled craftspeople recreate traditional Khmer silk weaving, stone carving, and lacquerwork.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant Kandal Village — a hip, locally-curated neighborhood filled with independent boutiques, galleries, and cafés. Browse local art and fashion, and enjoy the relaxed evening atmosphere away from the tourist bustle.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel before the early departure ($4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Banteay Srei at a local roadside restaurant — fresh spring rolls, grilled fish, and rice for $5–8 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Marum Restaurant (a training restaurant supporting street youth) in Siem Reap — excellent Khmer food with a social mission. Budget $12–18 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is covered by your Angkor Pass (Day 3 of use). Hire your regular tuk-tuk driver for the day — negotiate a full-day rate of approximately $20–25 USD. The Landmine Museum charges a small entrance fee (~$5 USD) and is a deeply meaningful experience that provides important historical context for Cambodia's recent past.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Siem Reap for Phnom Penh by express bus or domestic flight. The bus journey takes approximately 5–6 hours ($10–15 USD) and offers scenic countryside views; a domestic flight takes 45 minutes ($60–90 USD). Book tickets in advance. If taking the bus, depart by 7:00–8:00 AM to arrive by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check in to your mid-range hotel (recommend BK Hotel or Amanjaya Pancam Hotel near the riverside). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia, featuring stunning Khmer architecture, the Throne Hall, and a pagoda with a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles and a famous Emerald Buddha.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the scenic Sisowath Quay (the Phnom Penh Riverfront promenade) as the sun sets over the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. This is the social heart of the capital. Enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant watching the boats drift by.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Siem Reap hotel or grab food at the bus station before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus (pack snacks) or stop at a roadside restaurant en route — simple Cambodian rice dishes for $3–5 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (another excellent training restaurant) near the riverfront — specializing in traditional Cambodian recipes including countryside dishes. Budget $12–18 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Giant Ibis Bus is the most reputable and comfortable bus operator for the Siem Reap–Phnom Penh route. Book online in advance. Royal Palace is closed on Monday mornings and during official ceremonies — entrance fee is $10 USD. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for the Royal Palace.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a detention and torture center by the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). This deeply moving and historically essential museum documents the atrocities of the Khmer Rouge period. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough, respectful visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields) — located 15 km south of Phnom Penh, this is the most significant of the mass grave sites used by the Khmer Rouge. The memorial stupa and audio guide provide a profound and important historical experience. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco yellow dome building from 1937. Browse local goods, textiles, and souvenirs. Then enjoy dinner in the lively BKK1 neighborhood, Phnom Penh's cosmopolitan dining district.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at a nearby bakery — Phnom Penh has excellent French-influenced baguette and café culture from its colonial era ($4–6 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch near the National Museum at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a pioneering social enterprise training restaurant with excellent Khmer-fusion food. Budget $8–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner in BKK1 at Topaz Restaurant or Khéma for a slightly upscale Cambodian or French-Cambodian fusion dinner. Budget $15–22 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng entrance fee: $5 USD. Choeung Ek entrance fee: $6 USD (includes audio guide — highly recommended). These are emotionally heavy sites — allow time for reflection. The tuk-tuk round trip to Choeung Ek from the city costs approximately $10–15 USD. Visiting both sites in one day is intense but provides essential historical context for understanding modern Cambodia.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Phnom Penh for Sihanoukville (or directly to Koh Rong Samloem island). Take a bus to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours, $8–12 USD) or consider a direct tourist van. From Sihanoukville port, take a speed boat to Koh Rong Samloem (approximately 45 minutes, $25–30 USD round trip). Alternatively, head to Kep or Kampot for a more relaxed coastal experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and relatively unspoiled islands. Check in to a mid-range bungalow or guesthouse on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. Spend the afternoon swimming in the crystal-clear turquoise water, relaxing on the pristine white sand beach, and snorkeling over the coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular sunset from the beach. After dark, look for bioluminescent plankton in the shallows — a magical natural phenomenon common on this island. Enjoy a beachside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Phnom Penh hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or at a small café near Sihanoukville port before boarding ($5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood dinner at a beachside restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled whole fish, prawns, and rice with tropical fruit. Budget $10–15 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your island accommodation well in advance as mid-range options on Koh Rong Samloem fill up quickly. Recommended guesthouses: Lazy Beach Resort or The Village. Ferry schedules are weather-dependent — November is generally dry season with calm seas. Bring cash as ATMs are limited or unavailable on the island. Pack sunscreen, insect repellent, and any medications you need.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day on Koh Rong Samloem. Wake up early and walk along the pristine beach at sunrise — a magical experience with few other tourists. Rent a kayak or paddleboard from your guesthouse and explore the coastline, hidden coves, and mangrove channels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a snorkeling trip organized by your guesthouse or a local operator to explore the surrounding coral reefs and marine life. Alternatively, hike through the island's jungle interior to reach the secluded Sunset Beach on the western shore — a beautiful 45-minute walk through lush tropical forest. Relax on the uncrowded beach and swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saracen Bay for sunset. Try to spot the bioluminescent plankton again after dark — wade or swim in the shallows for a truly unforgettable experience. Enjoy a relaxed beachside dinner and stargazing.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse — tropical fruit, eggs, and coffee ($4–6 USD).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach shack or pack snacks for the hike — fresh coconuts, fruit, and sandwiches ($4–7 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at your guesthouse or another beachside restaurant — try Khmer-style steamed fish with ginger and lemongrass ($10–14 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rong Samloem has limited electricity (often solar-powered) and limited Wi-Fi — embrace the digital detox. Bring a good book and enjoy the slow pace. Snorkeling equipment can be rented for $5–8 USD/day. The hike to Sunset Beach is straightforward but wear proper footwear and bring water. The bioluminescence is best viewed on darker nights away from artificial light.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry back from Koh Rong Samloem to Sihanoukville. From Sihanoukville, travel to Kampot — a charming, laid-back riverside colonial town approximately 2.5 hours away by minivan or taxi ($8–15 USD). Kampot is famous for its pepper plantations, French colonial architecture, and the nearby Bokor Hill Station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kampot's charming Old Town — stroll along the riverside promenade, admire the French colonial buildings, and visit the Old Market. Then rent a bicycle or motorbike and visit one of the famous Kampot pepper farms (La Plantation or Sothy's Pepper Farm) for a guided tour learning about the world-renowned Kampot pepper — a UNESCO-recognized Geographical Indication product.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Kampot River — a classic Kampot experience. Many guesthouses and tour operators offer relaxed boat trips along the river as the sun sets behind the Elephant Mountains. Enjoy the peaceful scenery with a cold drink in hand.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your island guesthouse before the ferry departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kampot Old Town upon arrival — try Rikitikitavi Restaurant or Rusty Keyhole for excellent food in a colonial setting. Budget $7–12 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Epic Arts Café (a social enterprise supporting people with disabilities) or Baraka Restaurant for fresh Cambodian-Western fusion food. Try dishes featuring Kampot pepper. Budget $10–15 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Kampot accommodation in advance — recommended mid-range options include Mea Culpa Boutique Hotel or Teakwood Kampot Hotel. The pepper farm tour typically costs $5–10 USD and includes tasting. Sunset river cruise costs approximately $8–15 USD per person. Kampot is a wonderful, relaxed contrast to the busy temple and city days earlier in the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Bokor Hill Station — a fascinating abandoned French colonial resort perched at 1,075 meters above sea level in the Elephant Mountains. Take a tuk-tuk or motorbike taxi up the winding mountain road. Explore the eerie ruins of the old Bokor Palace Hotel, the old church, and the casino — now partially reclaimed by the jungle. The views over the Gulf of Thailand are spectacular on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kampot for lunch and last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up some authentic Kampot pepper (black, red, or white), locally made products, and handicrafts. Then travel back to Phnom Penh by bus or shared taxi (approximately 3–3.5 hours, $8–12 USD) for your onward journey, or relax in Kampot for one final afternoon by the river if your flight allows.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Cambodia — if back in Phnom Penh, enjoy a farewell dinner along the Sisowath Quay riverfront. Reflect on your incredible 10-day journey through Cambodia's ancient temples, tragic history, vibrant culture, and stunning beaches. Consider visiting a rooftop bar for sunset cocktails over the Mekong.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Kampot guesthouse — eggs, baguette, tropical fruit, and Cambodian iced coffee ($4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Final Kampot lunch at Neak Cafe or Greenhouse Restaurant — relaxed riverside setting with excellent food ($8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Phnom Penh at a riverside restaurant — splurge slightly on your last night. Try Khmer BBQ or a refined Cambodian tasting menu at Kravanh Restaurant. Budget $18–25 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Bokor Hill Station entrance fee is approximately $5 USD. A tuk-tuk or motorbike up to Bokor costs $15–20 USD round trip. Bring a light jacket as it can be cool and misty at altitude. Confirm your return transport to Phnom Penh in advance. If flying out on November 25, ensure you're back in Phnom Penh with enough time — the airport is about 30 minutes from the city center. Overall tip: Cambodia is a country of extraordinary beauty, deep history, and remarkable resilience — engage respectfully with locals and support community-based tourism enterprises wherever possible.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation at the hotel with a dedicated concierge. Enjoy a leisurely poolside welcome drink and light refreshments. Take a gentle introductory stroll through the immediate hotel grounds to acclimate to the atmosphere and recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace with views over the surrounding temple landscape. Enjoy a relaxed, curated welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant to ease into the journey.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread and afternoon tea prepared by the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the hotel's fine-dining restaurant — expect Khmer tasting menu with locally sourced ingredients, paired with curated Cambodian wines and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in preparation in advance. Ask the concierge to brief you on the next 10 days and confirm all private guide bookings. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private guided sunrise visit to Angkor Wat — arrive before 5:30 AM to secure a prime reflection pool position. Your expert archaeologist guide will walk you through the history, iconography, and symbolism of the world's largest religious monument as the sun rises behind its iconic towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-breakfast exploration of Angkor Thom complex — visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, Terrace of the Leper King, and Baphuon Temple. Travel by private air-conditioned vehicle with your dedicated guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to hotel for a late-afternoon spa treatment (traditional Khmer massage or aromatic oil therapy). Dinner at a premium Siem Reap restaurant in town — book a private dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast hamper prepared by the hotel, enjoyed near the Angkor Wat reflecting pools
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a heritage colonial-style restaurant near Angkor Thom — try the Amok fish curry and fresh spring rolls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak or Malis Restaurant, Siem Reap — both celebrated for refined modern Khmer cuisine using seasonal local produce

day_by_day.notes: Dress in lightweight, breathable clothing and bring sun protection. November weather is typically dry and pleasant (25–32°C). Pre-book sunrise temple access through your concierge for exclusive early entry.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Ta Prohm — the iconic jungle temple where massive silk-cotton trees intertwine with ancient stone galleries, famously featured in Tomb Raider. Enjoy the mystical atmosphere before the crowds arrive. Continue to Banteay Kdei and the sacred Srah Srang reservoir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive access visit to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' renowned for its extraordinary pink sandstone carvings and intricate bas-reliefs. Located 25 km north of Siem Reap, this temple is considered one of the finest examples of Khmer artistry. Private vehicle transfer included.
day_by_day.evening: Apsara dance performance dinner — attend an exclusive private or semi-private Apsara cultural performance at a heritage venue, watching Cambodia's ancient royal court dance tradition, a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, Khmer congee, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch prepared by the hotel, enjoyed in the shade near Banteay Srei temple gardens
meals.dinner: Set dinner accompanying the Apsara performance — multi-course Khmer royal cuisine featuring amok, lok lak, and banana blossom salad

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a 45-minute drive — depart by 9:00 AM to maximize time. Photography at Ta Prohm is spectacular in morning light. Ask your guide about the mythology behind each temple's carvings.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot-air balloon experience over the Angkor Archaeological Park — float above the jungle canopy and temple rooftops for a breathtaking aerial perspective of the entire complex at golden hour. Champagne served on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the lesser-known but magnificent Preah Khan temple — a vast 12th-century monastery and university complex with long atmospheric corridors, carved nagas, and hidden courtyards. Follow with Neak Pean, the mystical island temple set in an artificial lake.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on Tonlé Sap Lake — board a luxury private boat as the sun sets over Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Observe floating villages and extraordinary birdlife. Sunset cocktails and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Champagne and light breakfast pastries served during or after the hot-air balloon flight
meals.lunch: Lunch at a curated riverside restaurant in Siem Reap — fresh Tonlé Sap fish dishes, grilled river prawns, and Khmer herb salads
meals.dinner: Dinner aboard or post-cruise at a premium lakeside restaurant — fresh seafood tasting menu with Cambodian craft beer and wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon flights are weather-dependent — your concierge will confirm the evening before. Tonlé Sap Lake is at its fullest and most dramatic in November (post-monsoon season), making this the ideal time to visit.

day_by_day.morning: Cultural immersion morning — private visit to Artisans Angkor workshop and silk farm. Watch master craftspeople restore ancient Khmer artistic traditions including lacquerwork, stone carving, silver work, and silk weaving. Opportunity to purchase authentic, ethically made luxury souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Angkor National Museum for a deep-dive into Khmer civilization history, followed by a private guided walk through the old French Quarter of Siem Reap — explore colonial architecture, Buddhist temples, and the vibrant Psar Chaa (Old Market) area.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private cooking class with a celebrated Cambodian chef — learn to prepare three traditional Khmer dishes using ingredients sourced from the local morning market. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — Khmer-style rice porridge with ginger, fried egg, and fresh herbs alongside continental options
meals.lunch: Lunch at a boutique café in Siem Reap's French Quarter — fusion Khmer-French cuisine, fresh baguettes, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private cooking class, enjoyed in an intimate garden or villa setting with wine pairings selected by the chef

day_by_day.notes: The Artisans Angkor silk farm visit requires a 30-minute drive to Puok village — confirm timing with your concierge. Purchases at Artisans Angkor directly support local artisan employment programs.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered flight or premium transfer from Siem Reap to Sihanoukville (or Koh Rong Samloem island) — approximately 1-hour flight. Check in to a luxury overwater villa or beachfront resort on Koh Rong Samloem, Cambodia's premier island destination.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into your island accommodation and enjoy a private beach afternoon — snorkeling in crystal-clear turquoise waters, lounging on pristine white sand, or kayaking along the coastline. The island's bioluminescent plankton makes evening swims magical.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails on your private beach terrace. Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant under the stars — fresh catch of the day, lobster, and tropical fruits.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before departure — full spread with tropical fruits, pastries, and eggs
meals.lunch: Light lunch upon arrival at the island resort — fresh coconut, grilled fish, and tropical salads
meals.dinner: Beachfront fine dining at the resort — grilled lobster, Cambodian seafood curry, and fresh mango sorbet, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Book your island charter flight well in advance — limited seats. Pack reef-safe sunscreen and light linen clothing. November is ideal for Cambodian islands — dry season with calm seas and excellent visibility for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to the coral reefs surrounding Koh Rong Samloem — explore vibrant marine life including reef sharks, sea turtles, and tropical fish. PADI-certified dive master accompanies the group.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island on foot or by private longtail boat — visit the secluded Lazy Beach or M'Pai Bay fishing village for an authentic glimpse of island life. Optional: paddleboard yoga session on the calm lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton night swim — a once-in-a-lifetime experience where the ocean glows electric blue around you in the darkness. Best experienced on dark moon nights in calm waters.

meals.breakfast: Tropical breakfast served on your villa terrace — fresh papaya, coconut pancakes, Cambodian iced coffee, and tropical juices
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ lunch at a secluded cove during your boat excursion — freshly grilled fish, prawns, and salads
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner on the beach — chef-curated five-course tasting menu with wine pairing, celebrating the natural beauty of the island

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescence is most vivid during new moon phases — your concierge will advise on optimal timing. Bring waterproof bags for electronics during boat excursions. Respect marine conservation guidelines around coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga and meditation session on the private beach with a dedicated wellness instructor. Follow with a luxury spa morning — choose from a traditional Khmer herbal compress massage, deep tissue treatment, or a couples' spa journey using locally sourced botanical ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return boat transfer to Sihanoukville followed by a premium vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 3.5 hours) or a short domestic flight. Check in to a luxury hotel in Phnom Penh — recommended: Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal.
day_by_day.evening: Orientation stroll along the Phnom Penh riverfront promenade at sunset — watch the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers glow in golden light. Cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the illuminated Royal Palace.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast — smoothie bowls, fresh fruit platters, and eggs to order on your villa terrace
meals.lunch: Lunch en route or at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh upon arrival — Khmer noodle soup, fresh spring rolls, and sugarcane juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant or Malis Phnom Penh — refined Cambodian and French-Khmer fusion cuisine in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: If traveling by road, the scenic Phnom Penh–Sihanoukville expressway offers a comfortable premium vehicle experience. Pre-arrange hotel check-in time to ensure your room is ready upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Deeply moving and historically essential visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. A private expert guide will provide thoughtful historical context. Follow with a visit to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, 15 km from the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex — admire the Throne Hall, the Emerald Buddha, and the stunning Silver Pagoda floor laid with 5,000 silver tiles. Continue to the National Museum of Cambodia to view the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise along the Mekong River — champagne and canapés as the city skyline lights up. Dinner at a premium rooftop restaurant with panoramic views over the river.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel — buffet and à la carte options, fresh tropical fruits, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a refined restaurant near the Royal Palace — try kuy teav (Cambodian noodle soup) or beef lok lak with a fresh lime and pepper dipping sauce
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sora Sky Bar (Rosewood) or a premium rooftop venue — contemporary Cambodian cuisine with panoramic Mekong views and craft cocktails

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow time for reflection. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees) for the Royal Palace. Book the Mekong sunset cruise in advance through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Phnom Penh — visit the vibrant Central Market (Phsar Thmei) for last-minute luxury souvenir shopping: Cambodian silk scarves, silver jewelry, handmade crafts, and premium Kampot pepper. Explore the French Colonial Quarter's elegant boulevards and café culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell luxury spa treatment at the hotel — choose a full-body Khmer herbal ritual or signature facial to refresh before your departure. Enjoy a final leisurely lunch in the city. Private transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport for your onward flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phnom Penh International Airport. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Cambodia's ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine island paradise.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — full à la carte spread with Cambodian specialties, pastries, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Final lunch at a beloved Phnom Penh institution — try Khmer BBQ, fish amok, or a French-Khmer fusion meal at a heritage colonial restaurant
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight — your concierge can arrange premium airport lounge access for a comfortable pre-departure experience

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Ask your hotel to prepare a farewell gift bag with local Cambodian specialties — Kampot pepper, palm sugar, and artisan crafts make wonderful keepsakes. Confirm airport transfer at least 24 hours in advance.
